structure_summary: Wilson p. 169 and Chart 18: the new airborne division numbered 8,505 officers and enlisted men, of whom approximately 2,400 were parachutists, with 401 trucks. official_designation: Airborne Division tables of organization and equipment, 16 December 1944 (Wilson)
structure_summary: Wilson: one glider infantry and two parachute infantry regiments; four artillery battalions (parachute and glider, authorized 75-mm pack howitzers, with a note that one glider artillery battalion could have 105-mm howitzers); antiaircraft artillery and engineer battalions; trucks 400 to 1,000; authorized strength 12,979, about 50 percent parachutists.

official_designation: Infantry Division, 1944/5 War Establishment (Nafziger 939BXIA, after Joslen)
structure_summary: Nafziger 939BXIA, 1944/5 section (printed page 3 of the internal-structure part), citing Joslen: three infantry brigades of three battalions each (nine battalions), a reconnaissance regiment, three towed field regiments (72 25-pdr guns), a towed anti-tank regiment, a light anti-aircraft regiment, three field companies with a field park company and bridging platoon, divisional signals, a machine-gun battalion, three brigade RASC companies and a divisional troops company, and three field ambulances. Personnel 18,347. Anti-tank guns are the sum of the 78 6-pdr and 32 17-pdr listed separately in that section (110). PIATs (436) and the listed small-arms, mortar and vehicle counts are not stored as authorized keys, because those keys are not in the vocabulary. Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, Appendix IV Part II (pp. 533-540, R670), describes the same three-brigade infantry-division structure for 21 Army Group but does not give a division authorized total.
template_note: There is no single official War Establishment number for a British division (II/233 is the infantry battalion, not the division). This row is compiled from Nafziger 939BXIA, which cites Joslen, not from a Personnel Staff Table or an official WE volume. Inferred valid_from: Nafziger heads the table “1944/5” with no day or month, so valid_from is the first day of 1944 (old value blank, new value 1944-01-01, reason: first day of the year named in that heading, rather than inventing a mid-1944 effective date). edition_date is the year 1944. AHQ Report No. 57 (R2220) gives official Canadian authorized totals as at 31 May 1945 of 18,075 (1st Canadian Infantry Division) and 18,093 (2nd and 3rd), which disagree with the 18,347 figure stored here; that disagreement is recorded on the Canadian unit_toe rows (conformance modified) rather than silently preferred. The widely quoted 18,347 figure has not yet been verified from Joslen’s own page. valid_to is left open. Airborne divisions, the 79th Armoured Division and independent brigades are not this template.

official_designation: Armoured Division, March 1944, Organization No. VII (Nafziger 939BXAA, after Joslen)
structure_summary: Nafziger 939BXAA, March 1944 Organization No. VII (printed pages 7-8), citing Joslen: one armoured reconnaissance regiment, one armoured brigade of three armoured regiments and a motor battalion, and one infantry brigade of three infantry battalions, with a towed RHA or field regiment, a self-propelled field regiment, an anti-tank regiment (two towed and two self-propelled batteries), a light anti-aircraft regiment, two field squadrons, a bridging troop and a field park squadron. Cruiser tanks 246 (Ellis, vol. I, Appendix IV Part II, names the cruiser tanks of this campaign as Shermans and Cromwells). The file also lists 63 light tanks, 27 anti-aircraft tanks, 27 observation-post tanks and 3 bridge-layers, which are not stored as authorized keys because there is no light-tank or specialist-tank key in the vocabulary and they are not added into medium_tanks. Artillery pieces are the 24 towed and 24 self-propelled 25-pdrs (48). Anti-tank guns are the 30 6-pdr and 24 17-pdr listed separately from the 24 17-pdr M10s, which are stored as tank_destroyers. No personnel total is printed in the file.
template_note: Authorized personnel is left blank: Nafziger 939BXAA prints none, and the widely circulated 14,964 figure is not used because it has not been verified from Joslen or an official War Establishment or Personnel Staff Table. Inferred valid_from: Nafziger says “March 1944” with no day, so valid_from is the first of that month (old value blank, new value 1944-03-01, reason: first day of the named month). AHQ Report No. 57 Appendix D gives official Canadian authorized totals as at 31 May 1945 of 14,579 (4th Canadian Armoured Division) and 14,781 (5th); those figures are recorded on the Canadian unit_toe rows (conformance modified) and are not written onto this template. A later May 1945 Organization No. VIII is outlined in the same Nafziger file without an equipment list and is not applied. The 79th Armoured Division is a unique specialist-armour formation and is not this template. Independent armoured and tank brigades are not this template.
